'''East Harlem''', also known as '''Spanish Harlem''' or '''{{lang|es|El Barrio}}''', and formerly '''Italian Harlem''', is a [[neighborhood]] of [[Upper Manhattan]] in [[New York City]], north of the [[Upper East Side]] and bounded by [[96th Street (Manhattan)|98th Street]] to the south, [[Fifth Avenue]] to the west, and the [[East River|East]] and [[Harlem River]]s to the east and north.<ref name=enc-nyc/><ref name=hot/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nyc.com/visitor_guide/el_barrio_spanish_harlem.75851/editorial_review.aspx |title=El Barrio (Spanish Harlem) New York City.com : Visitor Guide : Editorial Review |publisher=Nyc.com |access-date=September 19, 2012}}</ref> Despite its name, it is generally not considered to be a part of [[Harlem|Harlem proper]], but it is one of the neighborhoods included in Greater Harlem.<ref>[[Jeffrey S. Gurock|Gurock, Jeffrey S.]], et al. "Harlem" in {{cite enc-nyc2}}, p. 573.</ref>

The neighborhood has one of the largest [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic]] communities in New York City, mostly [[Puerto Ricans]], as well as [[Dominican Americans|Dominican]]s, [[Salvadoran Americans|Salvadorans]], [[Cuban Americans|Cuban]]s, and [[Mexicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Exploring the Latino Metropolis: East Harlem |url=https://scalar.usc.edu/works/latino-metropolis-a-brief-urban-cultural-history-of-us-latinos---1/east-harlem-1 |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=Exploring the Latino Metropolis: A Brief Urban Cultural History of US Latinos |language=en}}</ref> The community is notable for its contributions to [[Latin freestyle]] and [[salsa music]]. East Harlem also includes the remnants of a once-predominant [[Italian Americans|Italian community]], or Italian Harlem. The [[Chinese in New York City|Chinese]] population has increased dramatically in East Harlem since 2000.<ref name="Mays 2011"/><ref name="Barron 2013"/><ref name="APA 2012"/>

East Harlem has historically suffered from many social issues, such as a high crime rate, the highest [[unemployment|jobless rate]] in New York City, [[teenage pregnancy]], [[AIDS]], [[drug abuse]], [[homelessness]], and an [[asthma]] rate five times the national average.<ref name="nyc.gov">{{cite web |url=http://www.nyc.gov/html/dcp/pdf/pub/mnneeds_2012.pdf |title=Community District Needs |access-date=September 19, 2012 |website=[[Government of New York City]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130317001127/http://www.nyc.gov/html/dcp/pdf/pub/mnneeds_2012.pdf |archive-date=March 17, 2013}}</ref> It has the second-highest concentration of [[public housing in the United States]], behind [[Brownsville, Brooklyn]].<ref name="Mays 2011 2"/> East Harlem is undergoing some [[gentrification]], and in 2016 the city considered rezoning the area.

East Harlem is part of [[Manhattan Community Board 11|Manhattan Community District 11]], and its primary ZIP Codes are 10029 and 10035.<ref name="NYCPlanning"/> It is patrolled by the 23rd and 25th Precincts of the [[New York City Police Department]].<ref name="NYPD 25th Precinct"/><ref name="NYPD 23rd Precinct"/>
